pages.observed: Five frames 0.0 to 0.8s of a vertical illustrated airport pickup curb scene: phone UI showing Ride requested with a route, a white generic car entering from left, an airport sign, bench and teal suitcase, skyline behind. Caption in lower area from 0.6s reads the Waymo San Antonio sentence. Lower third of frame is empty dark asphalt.

Five frames 1.0 to 1.8s: the white roof-pod car travels from left edge into the pickup bay with a red brake glow. Phone still reads Ride requested and Finding a car. Caption stays on two lines mid-frame. Lower half of frame is empty dark road.

Exterior bay frames at 2.0 and 2.2s then a cut to an interior cab at 2.4s showing the steering wheel, dash map screen and two empty front seats with no person. The phone overlay stays at upper left and the Texas outline card appears at upper right. Caption is the same two lines.

Interior cab view held across 3.0 to 3.8s: the steering wheel turns by itself with seats empty, the airport sign slides away behind the windshield pillar, and the small Texas outline card completes its trace. The phone overlay and caption are unchanged.

Four interior cab frames from 4.0 to 4.6s with little change, then at 4.8s a hard cut back to the curb where an enlarged tilted phone showing Ride requested overlaps the car in the bay. Caption is absent in the last frame. Texas outline card with a tiny orange point at upper right.

Five frames 5.0 to 5.8s: the enlarged tilted phone overlaps the front half of the white car at the bay. Its status text flips from Ride requested to Arriving At the curb at 5.6s and the route pin reaches the end. Caption reads the airport included. A road band is drawn across the lower frame with empty dark space below.

At 6.0s caption reads the airport included then vanishes; frames 6.2 to 6.6s show an unchanged curb with Arriving status. At 6.8s the picture cuts to a brown wooden desk seen from above with a cream paper map, three pins and a small calendar page reading February, with a blank gradient sky above and empty dark field below.

A tilted-perspective desk with a cream paper map and February calendar tab. Map is mostly blank for 7.0 to 7.4s, then orange street lines and blue river lines begin drawing from 7.6s. Pins are tiny. No car appears. Caption reads The service began in February. Map content is small relative to the frame.

The map fills with orange street lines and blue river lines and an orange oval outline traces around the central pins over 8.0 to 8.8s. The Texas outline card at top right fades out at 8.0s. Still no car and no tag for sixty square miles yet. Caption still The service began in February.

Between 9.0 and 9.2s the map view jumps closer and the February page drops onto the map and then moves around over 9.4 to 9.8s, covering the pins at times. Caption changes to in a limited area of sixty square miles at 9.4s. A thin black line starts to draw above the orange oval. No sixty square miles tag is shown yet.

A held close map view with the orange oval limited area already drawn and the February page parked lower left. Only a thin black polyline over the top of the oval grows slightly across the five frames. No car pin visible and no sixty square miles tag or numeral shown on the map. Caption reads in a limited area of sixty square miles.

Black outline closes into a polygon around the three pins and shades grey while a tag 60 square miles Limited area lands at the top of the map. A larger orange oval and the February page remain in view, so two different rings are drawn. No car icon is on the map. Caption reads in a limited area of sixty square miles.

Two held map frames, then at 12.4s a cut to a rainy brown creek with a small white car floating mid-frame and limestone ledges at right. The car is small in the frame and its cabin is not readable. Disclosure badge changes to a different car April 20th account. Caption appears at 12.8s. Upper half of the frame is empty sky.

Five nearly identical frames of a small white car sitting low in brown water at mid-frame with a faint reflection, rain falling, limestone steps at right. The car is roughly one third of the frame width and its cabin windows are tiny. The sweeping motion is barely visible across 13.0 to 13.8s. Large empty sky above and empty brown water below the caption.

Four wide frames repeat the small half-submerged car with almost no change, then at 14.8s a closer shot enlarges the car to about half the frame width with a wake and a reflection, trees larger above. Cabin windows still show no clear person or empty seat detail. Caption unchanged throughout.

Medium side view of the white car floating low with a visible wake at its right end, seat headrests visible through the windows and a reflection below. Across five frames it moves only a small distance rightward and rotates slightly by 15.8s. Tree and bush occupy the upper area. Caption unchanged. Lower third is brown water with rain strokes.

Medium side view: the white car with a visible tan mud line travels across the brown water, drifting left across the five frames with a wake line and spray at its front and rain falling. Windows show seat headrests and no person. Caption unchanged. This is the clearest depiction of a car being carried along water.

At 17.0 and 17.2s the creek car is at the left edge, then at 17.4s a cut to a suburban street with low beige houses, a green street sign and a white car with its wheels at the edge of a brown puddle. Floodwater covers only the left part of the road. Car is small and about a quarter of frame width. Big empty sidewalk fills the lower third.

The brown water rises across the whole road by 18.4s and the white car sinks until its wheels are covered by 18.8s. Car is small, windows too tiny to show any empty seat. No hazard lights seen yet. Caption unchanged. The empty sidewalk fills the lower third of the frame.

Amber hazard lamps flash on the small stranded car at 19.2 and 19.4s, then the camera closes in at 19.8s: the car is large with water at its wheel arches, windows show seat shapes and the background goes soft. Lower third is a plain empty sidewalk under the caption.

Medium shot of the stopped white car with water at its wheel arches. Only the amber hazard lamps change across the five frames, glowing at 20.0, 20.4, 20.6 and 20.8s and dim at 20.2s. Windows show seat shapes, no person. Background is blurred. Lower third is empty paved sidewalk.

The stopped car with water at its wheel arches repeats unchanged across 21.0 to 21.8s except for blinking amber lamps. The caption disappears at 21.4s leaving the lower third as plain sidewalk. Same composition as the previous interval, so this scene has held on one view for about 2.5s with only hazard lamp changes.

After the flood frame at 22.0s the film cuts to a desk with an olive wall. A cream card titled Federal recall record leans to the right and is cropped by the frame edge, its field lines are blank and nothing writes in for 22.2 to 22.8s. The pen sits at the lower right corner. Caption Waymo filed a software recall begins at 22.6s. Large olive empty areas above and below the desk.

The card slides to the center and its field rows write in progressively. Recall type Software at 23.4s, Potential units affected 3,791 at 23.6s where the label text and the number visibly overlap, and a Summary row with the full recall sentence at 23.8s. Fields are very small type relative to the frame. Caption reads Waymo filed a software recall.

The recall card fills with small-print rows including the remedy under development and the interim remedy, all while caption still says Waymo filed a software recall. The remedy line and the weather and April 20th lines appear on screen already at 24.0 to 24.6s, well before they are spoken at 40s and 43s. At 24.8s the view cuts to a wider desk with a smaller card and a grid of dashed car outlines, four filled. Potential units label overlaps its number.

A grid of small white car icons fills row by row, nearly 80 icons by 25.8s, beside the small recall card. A hand with a rubber stamp enters from the top right from 25.4s and moves over the card by 25.8s. The card text is tiny. Caption reads that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars. No 3,791 counter tag is visible yet.

The icon grid is complete and the stamp lands on the recall card leaving an orange Software recall mark at 26.4s. A tag reading Nearly 3,800 vehicles and 3,791 potentially affected in the record fades in at the top left of the card and partly covers the card. All this reads at the right moment for the clause. Text on the card is very small and the tag covers part of its header.

Five frames with no visible change at all except the caption leaving at 27.6s. The icon grid, stamped card and counter tag are static for about 1.0s. Lower third is empty olive wall beneath the desk. Icon grid shows about 80 cars, not 3,791 or 3,800.

Desk frame at 28.0s, then at 28.2s a cut to a gray highway lane with a white car entering at left and a green verge below. At 28.6s a recall sentence card fades in over the sky. The disclosure badge now reads the recall wording, not a recorded event. The lane has no standing water visible yet. A broad empty olive grass field fills the lower third.

The car cruises with scrolling lane marks and no standing water visible anywhere in the 29.0 to 29.8s frames. The recall sentence card sits at the top. The car is about one third of frame width. Lower third is empty grass. Caption reads The recall says the software may let a car slow.

The car brakes with a red lamp while a gray standing-water puddle slides in from the right ahead of it across the lane. This shows slowing before water, matching the clause. The puddle is a gray blob at the edge of the frame and the car is about one third frame width. Lower third is empty grass under the caption.

Wide shot holds with the puddle at the right then at 31.6s cut to a large close side view of the car on dry-looking dark pavement with wavy white lines under the wheels. The window shows seats and no occupant. Caption switches at about 31.74s to then drive into standing water. A grey puddle tip starts entering at right at 31.8s. Lower third is grass.

Close side view of the car with its brake lamp lit while the standing water approaches from the right, reaching the front bumper by 32.8s. The word may on the card gets an orange highlight at 32.8s. The car does not yet roll into the water in these frames. The card is a block of fine text above the car.

The car rolls into the gray standing water: at 33.0s the front touches water, at 33.4 to 33.8s the front wheel is inside the water with splash dots and wake lines while the word may glows orange on the recall card. This is the signature roll-in action and reads at phone size. Lower third is empty grass.

Five frames of the white car moving through standing water with ripples, spray and wake lines and the highlighted word may on the card. The car stays at the same screen position while the road, water and wake move. The scene shows the roll-in but no crash or stop, consistent with the disclosure. Lower third is empty grass.

The roll-through-water continues to 35.4s, then at 35.6s a hard cut to a large close view of the recall card where every row is already shown, including the Remedy row reading The remedy is currently under development, plus Interim remedy and Interim update rows. The Software recall stamp overlaps the Recall type and Potential units rows so the 3,791 value collides with the stamp. Caption appears at 35.8s.

The Remedy row highlights in peach across 36.0 to 36.6s and a pen tip starts to enter at the right at 36.8s. The remedy line reads The remedy is currently under development, large enough to read at phone size. The Software recall stamp still sits across the Recall type row with the 3,791 value colliding underneath it. Lower third is empty olive.

A hand with pen enters from the right and points near the Interim remedy row rather than the highlighted Remedy row, then leaves at 37.6s. At 37.8s the card enlarges and a stamp in a hand comes down over the Software recall stamp near the top. The pen and stamp hands are drawn in tan skin tone with a denim cuff.

A large hand-held stamp slides down across the card from 38.0 to 38.4s, lands on the Remedy row at 38.6s printing an orange Under development mark that overlays the existing remedy text, and lifts at 38.8s. The arm and stamp cover much of the card while they travel. This is the signature consequence for the remedy line and reads at phone size.

The stamp hand lifts away by 39.4s leaving the card with a Software recall stamp and an Under development stamp across the Remedy row whose underlying text is partly covered. From 39.4s the frame holds static with no caption and no motion to 39.8s. Lower third is empty olive.

A wide parking lot with four small white cars in a row at the upper part of the asphalt and an April calendar tag plus Vehicle maps card on the left pole. No weather limits tag with cloud and rain icon appears in these frames. Cars are about one tenth of frame width each and the lower two thirds of the frame is empty gray asphalt. Frames are nearly identical from 40.0 to 40.8s.

The four tiny white cars stay still while a Weather limits tightened tag with a rain cloud icon slides in from the left over 41.4 to 41.6s and settles overlapping the April calendar tag. The tag arrives about 1.2s after the caption line begins. Cars are small and lower two thirds of frame is empty asphalt.

Five frames with no change. The weather tag, April page, maps card and four parked cars are identical across 42.0 to 42.8s, about 1.0s of held still while the caption stays on As an interim step Waymo tightened its weather limits. Lower half is empty gray asphalt.

Another 1.2s of an unchanged lot with tag, calendar and four parked cars, then a gentle push-in begins at 43.6s. No check marks and no calendar flip yet when the caption reaches April twentieth at 43.8s. Cars remain tiny and the lower half of the frame is empty gray asphalt.

The calendar page reads April 20 from 44.0s with a flip animation continuing in 44.2 to 44.4s, then settles. The four cars in the lot are unchanged and no check marks appear on them yet. Caption reads and every affected car had the update by April twentieth. Cars are small and the lower half is empty asphalt.

Check marks start to appear above the cars from the left at 45.4s, one car at a time at about 0.2s apiece, reaching two of four cars by 45.8s. Calendar and weather tag are unchanged. The cars are small and the lower half of the frame is empty gray asphalt.

The check marks complete across the four cars by 46.2s and the Vehicle maps card also gets an updated check. From 46.2 to 46.8s the picture is held unchanged. Only four cars stand in for every affected car. Cars are small, empty gray asphalt fills the lower half.

Check marks, calendar and weather tag hold unchanged from 46.2 to 47.6s, then at 47.8s the film cuts back to the airport curb of the opening with the white car parked at the bay and the phone reading Arriving At the curb. Disclosure badge reads A generic airport ride, not the flood cars. No caption on the last frame. Lower third is empty dark asphalt.

The curb scene from the opening returns with the white car parked in the bay. The rear door starts to open at 48.6s and is open wider at 48.8s showing a dark cabin interior. Phone says Arriving At the curb. Caption So the airport ride is open appears from 47.94s. The lower third is empty dark road.

The rear door of the white car stands open with a tan and dark interior visible and no person appears from 49.0 to 49.8s. Frame is otherwise unchanged. The caption leaves after 49.6s. Lower half is empty dark road with dashed center line.

A reframed curb view with the car door open and a small recall record card lying flat on the road in the lower middle area, readable only as a small card with a stamp. Card text is tiny at phone size. The car, bench and phone are static from 50.0 to 50.8s. Large empty dark asphalt occupies the lower half.

The recall card scales up from small to about two thirds of frame width across 51.0 to 51.6s with the Remedy row highlighted in peach and the Under development stamp at its corner, then holds at 51.8s. The car with open door and the curb props stay still above it. This is the closing pairing of ride and record and reads at phone size, though the card lies on the road surface in front of the car.

The closing composition holds static for the full 52.0 to 52.8s: open-door car and curb props above, a legible recall card with the remedy under development below. Caption shifts at 52.6s to as currently under development. No motion appears anywhere in these frames. Lower third is empty dark road.

A split frame: the open-door car at the curb in the upper half and the desk in the lower half with the recall card and the phone side by side. A black underline draws beneath the remedy text from 53.2s to 53.8s. The card text is large enough to read at phone size. Lower third is empty wood desk.

The same split composition is held with no visible movement for 54.0 to 54.8s. The last caption leaves at about 54.04s so the remaining frames are uncaptioned and unchanging. This is the held closing image, running from about 52.0s to 54.8s of near-stillness. Lower third is empty wood desk.

Five identical frames of the split closing image with no caption, no motion and no text change from 55.0 to 55.8s. Voice has ended at 54.04s per captions so this is silent held picture before the credits. Lower third is empty wooden desk.

Credits page on a near-black field with the Texas flag mark, Texas AI Docket wordmark and texasaidocket.com link, then source lines Waymo October 14th, NHTSA recall 26E026, Texas Public Radio May 10th and 13th, an illustration note, a map note and the music credit with CC BY 4.0. The credit lists TPR dates May 10th and 13th. Lower half of the frame is empty dark.
Identical static credits card across 57.0 to 57.8s. Same text block as before, small type, left aligned, with the lower half of the frame empty and dark.
Identical credits card across 58.0 to 58.8s with all credit text unchanged and no motion. Lower half of the frame empty and dark.
Identical credits card across 59.0 to 59.8s, no motion, same text block and empty dark lower half.
Identical credits card across 60.0 to 60.8s, no motion, same text block and empty dark lower half.
The last frame of the film, 60.967s frame 1829, is the same credits card as the preceding five seconds, fully legible, with the full source and music credit and the empty dark lower half.
